rule.trigger: rainfall1Day >= 1 inch at >=20% of reporting rain gauges, or a flow crossing of its ledger high threshold
rule.end: 72 hours after all crossing gauges are observed below threshold, capped at t0 + 10 days
rule.daily_precision: Daily means can identify a trigger day only; its UTC midnight is a window boundary, not an observed crossing time.

hypotheses.text: The upper-Llano rain chiefly increased flow toward reservoirs, with a smaller Edwards response in the available daily records.
hypotheses.evidence: Comal daily mean was 136 cfs on 2026-10-01; the separate EAA summary reports 147 cfs on 2026-10-02, so a later response cannot be ruled out. Barton Springs reached 26.5 cfs at 2026-10-02 04:00 UTC and remained at percentile 17.412 against its daily record. Fifteen recharge-zone wells had a median seven-day change of -0.11 ft in the available pairs ending 2026-10-01. Llano volume was 15,216.9 acre-feet from 2026-09-29 11:00 UTC through 2026-10-02 11:00 UTC. Gauge flow does not measure reservoir storage gain or aquifer recharge.

hypotheses.text: Pressure transmission contributed more than storage recovery to J-17’s rapid rise.
hypotheses.evidence: J-17 daily high rose from 638.33 ft on 2026-09-30 to 640.07 ft on 2026-10-01, a 1.74 ft change. The EAA summary dated 2026-10-02 reports a 639.0 ft ten-day average; the saved stage comparison is Stage 3 and agrees with the EAA’s stated 35% reduction. The daily-high sequence from September 18 through October 1 is attached. Water levels alone do not establish the pressure-versus-storage mechanism.

conditions.meaning: Which trigger each 10-day average sits below, read against the transcribed EAA stage table. The EAA declares stages; this is the arithmetic, shown beside what the EAA page states.

stage_table_provenance.how_obtained: The thresholds are published only as images on that page. The images were captured verbatim on 2026-10-01 (sha256 below) and transcribed by the session that captured them. Verify against the 2025 CPM plan PDFs captured beside them (data/raw/eaa/cpm/) before quoting. The EAA declares stages from 10-day averages; this file only records the trigger table.

hypotheses.text: Paved catchments produced shorter pulses than limestone catchments; rainfall above about two inches may explain which limestone creeks responded.
hypotheses.evidence: Shoal peaked at 541 cfs on 2026-10-01 19:50 UTC; Walnut at 650 cfs at 19:30 UTC. Bull peaked at 14.9 cfs at 17:50 UTC and reported 0.43 cfs on 2026-10-02 12:00 UTC. Barton at Loop 360 peaked at 0.05 cfs on 2026-10-02 10:30 UTC. City gauges had a median 1.5-inch rainfall1Day total in the October 2 snapshot. The two-inch condition is a hypothesis, not a computed threshold. Missing baselines, long gaps and the literal zero-start recession rule prevent the response classes from establishing the proposed contrast.

hypotheses.text: Travis’s daily elevation response lagged the Llano flow pulse.
hypotheses.evidence: Llano at Llano passed 15,216.9 acre-feet from 2026-09-29 11:00 UTC through 2026-10-02 11:00 UTC; the last captured flow was 17,774 cfs at that endpoint. Travis rose from 674.75 ft on September 28 to 674.85 ft on October 2, a 0.10 ft change. Using September 29’s 674.65 ft instead gives the handoff’s 0.20 ft, but that daily value has no recorded clock time. Daily elevations cannot establish the order of changes within a day; later recorded elevations are needed to test the lag.

Travis.lake_window: through latest daily reading, including lag after storm
